facts.fact: The document, the National Digital Development Policy 2021 (a whole-of-government, whole-of-society policy across ten focus areas covering the digital economy and digital government), calls itself 'launched' in its unsigned foreword; it names no adopting act or body, and its design section records draft-policy consultation workshops held 28 September to 1 October 2021.

The policy is dated 2021 on its cover and states no end date for itself (only a 2039 middle-income vision), and the text is the document hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site mocti.gov.sl. Text public: yes.

The policy states that its Part 3 institutional framework spells out institutions, roles and mandates, listing a National Digital Development Council, a National Digital Development Agency, a Technical Working Group and a Partners Coordinating Committee; the captured text stops before Part 3, so the mandates themselves are not read.

The policy says it 'informs the development of' a National Digital Development Strategy that will set targets and roles, and its 2021 workshops collected initial thoughts to shape that strategy; no strategy text, adoption or drafting stage is stated.
